decisionUnit: An additional living-wage job placement attributable to the Center within the reporting year

bottomLine.interpretation: The FY2024 Economic Development allocation divided by 30 reported living-wage placements is a $42,942 gross reconciliation benchmark, not a causal or marginal impact price. If 25% of reported placements were additional because of the Center, the conditional midpoint would be approximately $171,768 per additional placement. A 10%-50% positive-attribution sensitivity spans approximately $85,884-$429,421. The external employment-services evidence is compatible with a null effect, so the true upper bound is not finite.

inputs.label: Illustrative gift
inputs.basis: Donor scenario, not published current funding room

inputs.label: FY2024 Economic Development allocation
inputs.basis: Audited functional expense. It includes employment, financial, housing, and small-business work and is not an employment-program budget or marginal quote.
inputs.confidence: high for accounting; low for employment allocation

inputs.label: 2024 job seekers receiving employment support
inputs.basis: The 2024 Year in Review reports 400+ job seekers receiving drop-in, workshop, mentorship, and one-to-one support. We use the published floor; service intensity and unique-participant reconciliation are not reported.

inputs.label: 2024 reported living-wage placements
inputs.basis: The 2024 Year in Review reports 30+ community members securing living-wage employment. The wage threshold, retention, service pathway, comparison rate, and attribution are unpublished.

inputs.label: Conditional share of reported placements that was additional
inputs.basis: MFI decision scenarios, not evidence estimates. The range asks what the accounting would imply if 10%, 25%, or 50% of reported placements were additional because of the Center. A null effect remains plausible because the Center has no comparison group and a systematic review found employment-service effects negligible or statistically insignificant on average.

formula.rangeMethod: conditional positive-attribution sensitivity: favorable = 50% of reported placements additional; midpoint = 25%; small positive = 10%

nullEffectBoundary: The numeric range is conditional on some positive Center-attributable effect. The Center has not published a comparison rate, retained-employment follow-up, earnings change, or program-level cost. The external systematic review found employment-service effects negligible or statistically insignificant on average. If the Center did not change placement probability, or a gift replaced public or restricted funding, additional placements approach zero and no finite positive cost-effectiveness estimate exists.

fundingRoom.status: not published for the modeled pathway
fundingRoom.boundary: The $100,000 scenario is illustrative and linear. Individualized coaching enrollment is currently paused, the Career Connections newsletter is paused until Fall 2026, government grants supplied 55% of FY2024 revenue, and five exact city-contract matches overlap service areas. The Center has not published an employment-specific budget, committed funding, remaining gap, staffing or employer capacity, placement forecast, or displacement analysis for the next gift.
fundingRoom.requiredNext: Obtain a dated employment-program budget, restricted and public funding reconciliation, unique participant and service-intensity cohorts, wage threshold, 6- and 12-month employment and earnings outcomes, a credible comparison, and $100K, $1M, and $10M marginal cases.

excludedBenefits: QALYs, WELLBYs, lives saved, and a 10-QALY life-substantially-bettered conversion
Employment retention and earnings gains because neither is published for the 2024 placement cohort
Employer-side inclusion, confidence, social connection, financial counseling, homeownership, and small-business outcomes
Career-fair attendance, workshops, newsletters, drop-ins, and coaching contacts as if they were durable outcomes
Economic value of a placement because wage, hours, duration, taxes, benefits, and the counterfactual earnings path are unknown
